equation_request.abstract: In this note, we develop a bounded-error quantum algorithm that makes $\widetilde{O}(n^{1/4}\varepsilon^{-1/2})$ queries to a function $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{0,1\}$, accepts a monotone function, and rejects a function that is $\varepsilon$-far from being monotone. This gives a super-quadratic improvement compared to the best known randomized algorithm for all $\varepsilon=o(1)$. The improvement is cubic when $\varepsilon=1/\sqrt{n}$.

specification.problem: Monotonicity testing of f:{0,1}^n->{0,1} with one-sided error: always accept monotone f, reject eps-far f w.p. >=2/3, using Otilde(n^{1/4} eps^{-1/2}) queries via amplitude amplification over a random-edge violation checker.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: n=3 (index register 2 qubits, i in {0,1,2}, value 3 unused), a fixed small f given as an XOR oracle placeholder, one checker unitary and a fixed number k of Grover iterations, then measurement of x, i, flag and classical verification of the returned edge. Outside scope: the paper's actual algorithm achieving the n^{1/4}eps^{-1/2} polylog bound, the path or hypercube-line tester, exponential search over iteration counts when eps is unknown, and the Chakrabarty-Seshadhri / Khot-Minzer-Safra proofs.

symbols.domain: positive integer, n=3 for the small instance

symbols.meaning: distance of f from monotone (fraction of 2^n)
n-bit input; bit j is qubit j of register X (little-endian)
x with bit i set to b
probability that a uniformly random (x,i) is a violated edge
amplitude angle with sin^2 theta = p
violation indicator for the edge: f(x^{i\to 0})=1 and f(x^{i\to 1})=0

equations.label: Edge violation predicate
equations.description: An edge (x^{i->0}, x^{i->1}) is violated iff the lower endpoint has value 1 and the upper endpoint has value 0. It is independent of x_i, so the check queries both endpoints.
equations.justification: Definition of a monotonicity violation on a hypercube edge; the abstract only says the algorithm accepts monotone functions.
assumptions: f is queried through an XOR oracle on ancilla qubits
both endpoints are queried explicitly, giving 2 queries per check plus 2 for uncompute

equations.label: Checker unitary and success probability
equations.description: Hadamards on X and index registers (uniform over i requires n a power of 2 or a padded or rejected invalid index), then compute both oracle values into ancillas, a Toffoli with a negated control writes v into the flag, and the oracle calls are uncomputed. The flag=1 amplitude squared is p.
equations.justification: Construction proposed in the sketch; the exact checker of the actual paper is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: for n=3 an index value 3 is treated as nonviolating (v=0)
the normalisation then uses 4*2^n index-x pairs so p is rescaled by n/4

equations.label: Amplitude amplification
equations.description: Grover iterations Q=-U_check S_0 U_check^dagger S_flag, where S_flag flips the sign of flag=1, give this success probability. With p about eps/sqrt(n) this needs k=O(n^{1/4}eps^{-1/2}).
assumptions: p known or lower-bounded from assumed eps

equations.label: Edge density to iteration count
equations.description: Assumed per-edge violation probability for eps-far functions, matching the claimed query complexity up to polylog factors.
equations.justification: The query bound is consistent with amplifying a success probability of eps/sqrt(n) with O(1) queries per iteration. The edge-density bound itself comes from the Chakrabarty-Seshadhri / Khot-Minzer-Safra analyses, which is background not stated in the abstract.

equations.label: Verification and decision rule
equations.description: After measurement, the returned (x,i) is verified with 2 direct queries. Monotone f is always accepted.
equations.abstract_quote: accepts a monotone function, and rejects a function that is $\varepsilon$-far from being monotone
equations.justification: Accepting monotone f always is the one-sided error behaviour; the classical recheck is from the sketch.
assumptions: error reduction by constant repetition gives success >=2/3

registers.name: X
registers.role: input x, qubit j = bit j

registers.name: I
registers.role: edge direction index, uniform superposition by H

registers.name: A
registers.role: ancillas holding f(x^{i->0}) and f(x^{i->1}) temporarily, uncomputed to 0

registers.name: W
registers.role: work qubits for setting bit i to 0 or 1 (controlled on I) and for the multi-controlled gates; copy of x with bit i forced

specification.initial_state: All qubits |0>; U_check applies H to X and I.

steps.description: Apply Hadamards on X and I to make a uniform superposition over (x,i).

Compute the lower and upper endpoints (bit i forced to 0 and 1) into work copies controlled on I, query f on each via the placeholder oracle, and compute the flag by a Toffoli with negated control on the upper value. Uncompute the queries and copies, leaving the flag.
Apply k Grover iterations with the flag as marked bit (phase flip on F=1, then U_check^dagger, reflection about |0>, U_check).
Measure X, I, F, then classically query f at the two endpoints and apply the decision rule.

specification.measurement: Measure X (n bits), I (2 bits) and F. In a Qiskit counts key the last character is classical bit 0, so reverse the string before indexing. Use e.g. creg order [X bits, I bits, F].
specification.classical_postprocessing: For each shot with F=1, recompute v(x,i) from two direct oracle queries; reject if any verified shot is violated, else accept. Repeat O(log) times for error reduction.
assumptions: n=3 or 4 and a fixed small f chosen for the test, such as a non-monotone function with a few violated edges
k is fixed from an assumed eps or known p
the oracle is an XOR oracle, so it can be uncomputed
a padded index value (n not a power of 2) is treated as non-violating
polylog overhead and the path tester are omitted
missing_information: the actual algorithm of the paper, which is likely more refined than the edge tester
the precise sampling distribution or tester giving the polylog-optimal bound
how the paper handles unknown eps
the exact constants in the query count
